title: Records that were never issued
summary: Masters made in a New Orleans hotel with Bayersdorffer were never released.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: See? Dave Lewinner didn't come with us, uh, down there, down there. Oh, I see. So we had to merge our band with, uh, with Jack Tilson. Didn't, didn't Johnny tell you about Jack Tilson and them, when we played in the and out?
Probably did, but I've forgotten them.

But I'm just saying, I'm, I'm trying to... I've heard the name. ...trying to go from one stage to the next and then jump into the other, see? Yeah. But, uh, but those records, uh, were never produced. Just like we made some okay records in New Orleans with Johnny. And, and, uh, I don't know what the hell happened with those. The, the, uh, I can't think of the name of the recording man. He used to be with Victor Recording Company. Later on went back, back to Victor. Uh, I can't think of the recording manager. But we made it in some, some hotel or something.
Eddie, Keane. Well, anyway, uh, those, those records never did come out at that time, see? So, that, that, that, early, early time recordings.
Yeah, well, there were plenty of troubles with making records then. I know. Yeah. I had a hard time then.
